messages:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing prod GPU nodes fail to finish onboarding in usw3 starting ~12:40 UTC. Keystore decrypt errors in the node-init logs. Anyone digging?
maya: yep I'm on it, seeing `KMSDecrypt: Throttling` repeated, looks like a spike in KMS traffic.
sam: curious if this lines up with the audit shipper burst from the new egress retention test? we enabled full sampling at 00:00 UTC for the region.
lina: @maya can you paste the log snippet? also which firewall change shipped this morning? ops said an egress tighten rolled at 11:55.
maya: log: ```
2026-02-25T12:41:02Z node-init[pid=123]: keystore: decrypt failed: KMS: ThrottlingException (requestsPerSecond)
2026-02-25T12:41:03Z node-init[pid=123]: retrying decrypt (n=3)
2026-02-25T12:41:09Z node-init[pid=123]: decrypt succeeded after backoff
```
zack: firewall change was the default-eject egress ACL (deny all -> allow-list audit-shippers + privatelink). Shouldn't block KMS, KMS egress goes via natgw though.
alex: but if audit shipper flood saturated the natgw conntrack/QPS we might see proxied KMS calls drop/queue and cause retries -> provisioning lag.
ops-bot: alert: usw3 keystore QPS > 85% threshold for natgw-1 (12:39 - 12:46 UTC) :warning:
sam: quick check: S3 audit upload + KMS decrypts per node join = ~2-3 extra calls. At scale that multiplies. If retention test enabled across many hosts that could easily spike KMS.
lina: is there an immediate mitigation we can do to unblock GPU onboarding?
maya: short term: 1) pause full-sample audit shipper for usw3 (set sampling=0.1) 2) temporarily add keystore service to natgw high-priority route (allowlist) 3) increase keystore client retry backoff to reduce hammering.
security-bot: note: changing audit sampling affects compliance telemetry. If we drop below retention policy we need an incident ticket and exec signoff.
alex: understood, but customer-facing capacity is priority for the moment. we'll document and revert.
zack: ops: can you toggle sampling now? @sam can you make a quick PR to lower sampling and patch the shipper config in usw3?
sam: copying a config snippet I'll deploy to canary then roll: ```yaml
shipper.sampling: 0.1
shipper.targets: ["s3://audit-usw3/samples"]
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout start shipper-config/usw3 -> canary (rev b3)
lina: and I'll open a short-lived allowlist for KMS in the natgw routing policy, just the keystore IPs + kms endpoints.
alex: once that unblocks joins let's discuss medium-term: reduce KMS dependency on hot-path node init (ephemeral local encrypt + async KMS attest), and add quota-aware client in keystore.
maya: agree. Also we should look at audit retention vs egress cost — full sampling in multiple regions was the test; it danced up KMS + S3 egress costs.
zack: cost numbers rough: doubling sample rate in usw3 added ~1.2M KMS calls/day and ~$6k/day extra natgw egress.
security-bot: flag: any change to audit retention must be logged in compliance tracker ticket CT-4728.
sam: for now rolling sampling->0.1 in canary (12:50), if green will prod roll at 12:55.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary success shipper-config/usw3 (rev b3) -> healthy (12:53) :white_check_mark:
alex: good. owners: sam -> reduce sampling and coordinate rollback; lina -> natgw allowlist; maya -> monitor KMS QPS & node join rate; zack -> cost estimate and follow-up doc. I'll file the incident summary after stabilization.
maya: monitoring: KMS QPS dropped to 46% within 5m of config change, node join jitter down to baseline.
lina: natgw allowlist applied (12:54) — confirmed keystore-to-kms flows up.
zack: start a short postmortem? I'll draft cost/regression analysis.
alex: assign action items and close once onboarding returns to normal for 30m.
security-bot: reminder: don't forget CT-4728 update and retention policy exception if we stay below target sampling.
ops-bot: watch: will emit followup if natgw QPS > 80% again.
alex: thanks all — nice quick ops. We'll reconvene tomorrow to scope keystore async work. :thumbsup:
